error:
This report cannot be published yet -- 8 separate issue(s) found, ALL listed here so they can be fixed in one pass rather than one preview_report attempt per issue:
[1] validation refused: 7 claim(s) have no warehouse figure and no sign an outside check was attempted: "It's an unusually quiet conclusion to a season that defied expectations and broke a 121-year-old hurricane record."; "The hurricane drought ended Oct. 8, when Isaias became the Atlantic's first hurricane of the season, breaking a 121-year record for the latest first hurricane."; "10 named storms, the fewest since 2014, when there were only eight storms."; "The first record fell in September when the Atlantic went without a hurricane through Sept. 21, breaking a 112-year record."; "Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, at 8:30 p.m. CDT Friday, Oct. 9, as a Category 2 hurricane, peaking as a Category 3 with 120 mph winds."; "Isaias contributed to more than 20 tornadoes, and as many as eight people were killed by indirect storm impacts."; "AccuWeather preliminarily estimated $16 to $20 billion in total damage and economic loss from Isaias.". Finding nothing is acceptable; not looking is not. For each one, web_fetch the report, release or dataset the article cites or that would carry the figure (any outcome counts, a 403 or timeout included) and list that URL in the claim's `sources`, or run web searches for it and list the queries in `searched`. Fetching the article itself does not count. Then grade on what the check found.
[2] validation refused: 2 claim(s) about a named person or organization are graded 'unsupported' with no page read beyond the article: "AccuWeather estimated $4 to $6 billion in total damage and economic loss from Arthur."; "AccuWeather experts have declared that tropical activity for the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season is over; the weather patterns give confidence the United States will avoid additional direct tropical impacts this year.". web_fetch reporting or a record on it, list that URL in the claim's `sources`, then grade on what it says. If no page opens, list the pages tried in `sources` and say why in `why_no_page`; the verdict stays 'unsupported'.
[3] validation refused: the article https://www.yahoo.com/news/weather-news/articles/2026-atlantic-hurricane-season-over-191837658.html was not fetched with web_fetch in this session, so the sources it links are unknown. web_fetch it, then web_fetch every source it links, then publish again.
[4] validation refused: the article https://www.yahoo.com/news/weather-news/articles/2026-atlantic-hurricane-season-over-191837658.html did not load, so its claims were not read from its text. web_search the headline or a distinctive sentence for a copy of the same story (a syndication partner, the wire service, an archive), web_fetch it, extract the claims from that text, and name it in `article_copy_url`.
[5] validation refused: the assertion "It was also the first time since 1925 that there was only one hurricane in the entire season." names the measure "number of hurricanes per Atlantic season historical", but search_catalog was never called with that query this session. Run it, look at what it returns, and grade on that. ALSO: the assertion "AccuWeather estimated $4 to $6 billion in total damage and economic loss from Arthur." names the measure "Atlantic hurricane named storms HURDAT tropical cyclone", but search_catalog was never called with that query this session. Run it, look at what it returns, and grade on that. ALSO: the assertion "AccuWeather experts have declared that tropical activity for the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season is over; the weather patterns give confidence the United States will avoid additional direct tropical impacts this year." names the measure "Atlantic hurricane named storms HURDAT tropical cyclone", but search_catalog was never called with that query this session. Run it, look at what it returns, and grade on that.
[6] validation refused: 2 claim(s) of an attributed figure are graded 'unsupported' with no page read off the article's own site: "AccuWeather estimated $4 to $6 billion in total damage and economic loss from Arthur."; "AccuWeather experts have declared that tropical activity for the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season is over; the weather patterns give confidence the United States will avoid additional direct tropical impacts this year.". Search for other reporting or the primary record, web_fetch a page that loads and list it in `sources`, then grade on what it says. A Google Drive or Docs viewer page does not count. Grade each figure as its own claim. If no page loads, cite the off-site pages tried and say why in `why_no_page`.
[7] validation refused: check the claims against this procedure before publishing, then resubmit.

--- if you are fact-checking this page, follow this procedure ---
1. Get the article text. If the article's URL returns 403 or similar, web_search the headline for another outlet's copy (wire stories are syndicated) and web_fetch that copy. 2. Extract every assertion of fact into `claims`, one per assertion. Every comparative or streak phrase MUST be its own claim: "Nth straight", "lowest/highest since YEAR", "record", "on pace for", "first time since", "up/down from", "most since". Every attributed cause ("experts blamed X") MUST be its own claim. Mark exactly one claim `central`: the headline assertion. 3. For each claim, search_catalog for the measure it rests on and query it at the same unit and period. 4. A trend or streak claim MUST be tested against the level series at the article's own grain (month, quarter or year), across every period the phrase spans: "fifth straight yearly decline" needs the five year-over-year changes, "lowest since 2014" needs every period from 2014 on. Grade on whether the series shows that trend or only a one-period move. 5. A claim the warehouse does not carry (an agency's new release, a company announcement, a cited study) MUST still be graded from the primary source with web_fetch, and from web_search when the source is not linked. List the queries in `searched`. 6. The central claim MUST be graded on the evidence found, not 'not checkable here': web_fetch the release or report that published its figures and grade on it; when that page will not load, grade on copies that quote it. 'not checkable here' is only for a personal attack or a claim that is an opinion or belief no evidence can test ('chocolate chip cookies are the best cookies'), marked kind: opinion, with a reason saying in one sentence why no evidence can test it (an opinion of taste, a belief, or figurative speech); a missing table or a page that will not load never makes a factual claim uncheckable; when nothing found supports it, it is 'unsupported'. For an opinion that may imply a checkable fact ('politician A is a crook'), the claim's reason MUST state whether the speaker meant it literally, from the context. Meant literally ('has committed crimes'), the implied fact MUST be split out as its own claim, searched for (a criminal record) and graded; meant figuratively ('is dishonest'), it stays an opinion. 7. A figure the piece presents as a projection or early estimate MUST be graded on whether it matches the estimate the agency published, or the arithmetic of the components the agency published. A match MUST be graded 'true'; the figure being preliminary MUST NOT lower the verdict. The `reason` MUST say it is an estimate.
[8] no query call anywhere this session returned any rows -- askamerica's own data had nothing to contribute to this question. (The AskAmerica server restarted at 2026-11-16T12:47:16.569145Z and has no record of earlier calls: the record is kept across a restart only when the restart came within 10 minutes of the last call. Queries run before then are not lost, only unrecorded -- rerun the key queries now and they will be on record.) search_catalog, list_tables, and describe_table were NEVER called this session -- before falling back to the open web, actually check the catalog and confirm the gap is real, rather than assuming coverage is absent. Only 0 distinct URL(s) were fetched via web_fetch -- below even the bare minimum sanity-check floor of 5 this session enforces. A confirmed gap changes WHERE the answer comes from, not how hard to look for it: fetch and read enough distinct, substantive sources (actual documents, not search-result snippets) to make this an EXHAUSTIVE study for a question of this scope, not a passing amount -- where the question implies a full universe (every state, every facility, every county), that means attempting to enumerate it, not sampling a few examples. Clearing this floor is not itself evidence the research is complete, only that it isn't the worst failure mode measured in production. The connector having nothing to offer is never a reason to research less than you would with no connector at all.

args.query: number of hurricanes per Atlantic season historical
Atlantic hurricane named storms HURDAT tropical cyclone

sql: SELECT declaration_title, fema_declaration_string, declaration_date, COUNT(*) n FROM disasters.disaster_declarations WHERE "year" = 2026 AND (declaration_title LIKE '%ARTHUR%' OR declaration_title LIKE '%LALA%' OR declaration_title LIKE '%NOLO%') GROUP BY declaration_title, fema_declaration_string, declaration_date
